title: Expected shifts in thermal niche position of the Natura 2000 network for wintering waterbirds
content:
We presented the thermal niche position as an intuitive metric to be combined with other relevant parameters to do climate vulnerability assessments, and discussed how it has been used to plan future management efforts for the conservation of wintering waterbirds in Camargue (France). Overall, our study highlights the need for adapting the management of the Natura 2000 network to climate change.


Abstract

Climate change has strong effects on biodiversity, including species inside protected areas (PAs). Ensuring PA effectiveness despite species distribution shifts in response to temperature increase is challenging. In the European Union, waterbird conservation is targeted by the Natura 2000 (N2K) network of PAs. However, during winter, waterbirds are already moving northwards due to climate warming, increasing the risk of mismatches between hosted and legally targeted species. Here, we investigate the need for adapting conservation targets inside the whole N2K network for wintering waterbirds. We assessed PA exposure to climate warming at the end of the 21st century and translated it into a species-specific metric relative to species thermal niche, that is, the thermal niche position (TNP) of PAs for a specific species. PA exposure to winter temperature increase was systematic, ranging from +2.6 to +6.0°C by 2100 depending on climate scenarios. For waterbirds, the temperature increase translates into an average shift of +10% to +19% in TNP. The current N2K network will cover a much warmer part of the thermal niche of the species they are designated to target, particularly in eastern and northern Europe. Cold-dwelling species will be increasingly targeted at the warm distribution edge and warm-dwelling species will be less targeted at the cold distribution edge. If, as expected, climate warming induces population changes, PA managers may want to resist or facilitate changes. To help them in implementing climate adaptation strategies, we developed a web tool to pinpoint in every N2K PAs which target species might require specific attention, based on their TNP change. Synthesis and applications. We presented the thermal niche position as an intuitive metric to be combined with other relevant parameters to do climate vulnerability assessments, and discussed how it has been used to plan future management efforts for the conservation of wintering waterbirds in Camargue (France). Overall, our study highlights the need for adapting the management of the Natura 2000 network to climate change.
